recent_posts.title: Claude's Structured Outputs
recent_posts.summary: Anthropic's structured outputs for Claude allow LLMs to return validated, schema-conformant data via JSON schemas, transforming them from chatbot-style interfaces into deterministic, programmable components. This shift enables computer-to-computer communication rather than human-to-computer interaction, which is foundational for agentic AI systems that call APIs, read databases, and trigger workflows. Drawing parallels to historical enabling technologies like the telegraph relay, vacuum tube, Edison's electrical grid, and the transistor, the author argues that structured outputs are a quiet but pivotal inflection point — one that will unlock a wave of third-party innovation by developers who will discover applications the creators never imagined.

recent_posts.title: Why I'm No Longer Talking to Architects About Microservices
recent_posts.summary: Microservices discussions are often unproductive due to unclear definitions, abstract conversations disconnected from business goals, and lack of necessary organizational changes. Instead of focusing on microservices as an end, it's crucial to address concrete challenges like faster feature deployment, reducing system coupling, and scaling efficiently. Effective microservices implementation requires cross-functional, autonomous teams and a mature DevOps culture. Organizational change is harder than software change and essential for microservices' success.

recent_posts.title: Exploring OSCAL Using Neo4J
recent_posts.summary: An exploration of using Neo4J to visualize OSCAL (Open Security Controls Assessment Language) documents, highlighting the challenges of understanding OSCAL's jargon-heavy schema and the practical benefits of visualizing control relationships with graphs. The project aims to automate management and reporting of security controls with open source tools.

recent_posts.title: Paralysed by Perfection: the Case for Action in Times of Change
recent_posts.summary: Businesses often face paralysis by over-planning and fear of failure, which can hinder necessary changes for survival. Shifting from a comfort zone of predictable routines to embracing experimentation and risk-taking is crucial for innovation and growth. Leaders must support a culture of experimentation, incentivize risk-taking, and distinguish between reversible ('two-way door') and irreversible ('one-way door') decisions to navigate times of change effectively. Real-life examples highlight the importance of decisive action in uncertain contexts.

recent_posts.title: Does Crossplane Replace Terraform? Part I: the Theory
recent_posts.summary: Crossplane is a tool built on Kubernetes to orchestrate anything, and it can replace Terraform in certain scenarios. APIs are mechanisms for software components to communicate, while cloud services combine a remote network connection, an API, and delegation of responsibility. A control plane manages how work is done by a system.

recent_posts.title: In Praise of Low Tech DevEx
recent_posts.summary: The post discusses the concept of low-tech devex and its benefits. It emphasizes the use of long-standing, battle-hardened tools with stable histories, small dependencies, and text-based input and output. The post also highlights the portability, speed, power, composability, and user-friendliness of low-tech devex tools.

recent_posts.title: At 50 Years Old, Is SQL Becoming a Niche Skill?
recent_posts.summary: Opinions are divided on whether SQL is becoming a niche skill. Despite its historical demand and popularity, there is a rise in specialization in the IT industry, leading to the emergence of data scientists and other specialized roles. SQL remains widely used and is even implemented in alternative tools like DuckDB and osquery. However, some argue against the use of schemas in favor of more flexible databases like MongoDB.

recent_posts.title: OK Cloud, On-Prem is Alright
recent_posts.summary: Businesses are shifting from a wholesale 'migration to cloud' strategy to a more piecemeal, hybrid approach. This shift is motivated by experience, financial necessity, and the recognition of the importance of portability. The reasons for the retreat from wholesale cloud migration include migration exhaustion, cost of hardware, and macroeconomic trends. Despite the slowdown in the growth of cloud adoption, the cloud will continue to play a significant role, and smaller, cheaper, and interoperable cloud solutions will emerge.

recent_posts.title: Introducing the Open Source Compliance Framework
recent_posts.summary: Container Solutions has open sourced the Compliance Framework, an open source software suite designed to automate and manage business compliance tasks. It allows for continuous compliance, real-time reporting, and integration with OSCAL-compatible tools.

recent_posts.title: Cloud Cost Management Part II - Quick Wins
recent_posts.summary: This post discusses 'Quick Wins' in cloud cost management, including categories of savings, techniques for resource review, resource removal, resource usage, finops foundations, and commercial agreements with CSPs.
